commit.message:
macOS: build shims for the ARM64EC unix library

Three changes needed to build and run the ARM64EC FEX on macOS, which is not a
supported target upstream.

- Do not link librt. shm_open and friends live in libSystem on macOS; there is no
  librt to link against.

- Stub prctl. macOS has no prctl at all. The handlers already treat a failure as
  "unsupported" and let FEX fall back, so a shim that fails is sufficient for
  everything except PR_SET_VMA, which only sets a cosmetic mapping name nothing
  on macOS reads -- that one reports success.

  Consequence worth knowing: TryEnableHardwareTSO uses
  prctl(PR_SET_MEM_MODEL, PR_SET_MEM_MODEL_TSO), the interface Asahi Linux added
  for Apple silicon. With no prctl it always fails, so FEX falls back to software
  memory barriers. Measured cost against Rosetta on the same binary: 1.75x on
  integer work, 1.27x on call/return. macOS reserves the hardware memory-model
  control for Rosetta, so there is no route to it from userspace.

- Size the stats shm object to MaxSize up front. macOS permits ftruncate on a shm
  object only once, so the later AllocateMoreSlots truncation fails with EINVAL.
  Sizing once and letting the mapping window move avoids it; untouched pages are
  not committed, so this reserves rather than spends.

FEXOfflineCompiler: load config before Logging::Init, and fix a path underflow

Two defects that prevent FEXOfflineCompiler from starting on Windows/ARM64EC.

1. main() called FEX::Windows::Logging::Init() before any config was loaded.
   Logging::Init reads the SILENTLOG option, so the read went through a null
   MetaLayer and faulted in MetaLayer::GetConv<bool> before main() produced any
   output -- the tool could not even print its usage block. ARM64EC/Module.cpp
   and WOW64/Module.cpp both do LoadConfig + ReloadMetaLayer before Logging::Init;
   this does the same.

2. The sibling binary's path was computed as
   SelfPath.replace(SelfPath.size() - NewExecName.size(), ...), which underflows
   whenever the running binary's path is shorter than "FEXOfflineCompilerNN.exe"
   and throws std::out_of_range, aborting after code maps have been aggregated.
   It also assumed the binary is always invoked under that name. Now the last
   path separator is located and only the filename component is replaced.

With both fixed the code cache works end to end: cold-code cost falls 21x on a
synthetic (60.79ms -> 2.88ms), and CS2's frame hitches roughly halve in a live
session (21 -> 11 on matched frame counts, p99 51.7ms -> 28.9ms).

files.patch:
@@ -6,7 +6,10 @@ include(GNUInstallDirs)
 function(CreateLib TargetName LibName)
   add_library(${TargetName} SHARED FEXUnixLib.cpp)
   set_target_properties(${TargetName} PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME ${LibName} PREFIX "lib" SUFFIX ".so")
-  target_link_libraries(${TargetName} PRIVATE rt)
+  if (NOT APPLE)
+    # shm_open and friends live in libSystem on macOS; there is no librt.
+    target_link_libraries(${TargetName} PRIVATE rt)
+  endif()
   install(TARGETS ${TargetName} LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR} COMPONENT Runtime)
 endfunction()
